<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par58" />retraction of the tone before a following tone-syllable, but read certainly {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַר לָנֶ֫צַח}}.—The forms {{GHGheb|text=־֫מוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ מוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ מוֹ}} occur 23 times, all in poetry<ref>Thus in Ps 2 {{GHGheb|text=־מוֹ}} occurs five times [four times attached to a noun or preposition, {{GHGpar|91|f|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|103|c|nosign=1}}], and {{GHGheb|text=־ֵם}} only twice.</ref> (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=31}}) [viz. with the perfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=6}}; with the imperfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=מוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מוֹ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=7.9.9.12.15.17.17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=10.13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=10|hidebook=1}}; with the imperative {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=12.12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=12|hidebook=1}}]. On the age of these forms, see {{GHGpar|91|l}} 3; on {{GHGheb|text=־ַן}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָן}} as suffixes of the 3rd fem. plur. of the imperfect, {{GHGpar|60|d}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=קָֽחֶם־נָא}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכֶּם־שָׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=14|verse=11}} according to Baer), {{GHGheb|text=־ֵם}} has lost the tone before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} and so is shortened to {{GHGheb|text=־ֶם}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂימוּן}} is probably only an error for {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂימוּם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|h}}
2. From a comparison of these verbal suffixes with the noun-suffixes (§ 91) we find that (''a'') there is a greater variety of forms amongst the verbal than amongst the noun-suffixes, the forms and relations of the verb itself being more various;—(''b'') the verbal suffix, where it differs from that of the noun, is longer; cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=־֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נִי}} (''me'') with {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (''my''). The reason is that the pronominal object is less closely connected with the verb than the possessive pronoun (the genitive) is with the noun; consequently the former can also be expressed by a separate word ({{GHGheb|text=את}} in {{GHGheb|text=אֹתִי}}, &c.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|i}}
'''4.''' A verbal form with a suffix gains additional strength, and sometimes intentional emphasis, when, instead of the mere connecting vowel, a special connecting-syllable<ref>It is, however, a question whether, instead of a connecting syllable, we should not assume a special verbal form, analogous to the Arabic ''energetic mood'' (see l, at the end) and probably also appearing in the Hebrew cohortative (see the footnote on {{GHGpar|48|c}}).—As M. Lambert has shown in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 178 ff. (‘De l’emploi des suffixes pronominaux...’), the suffixes of the 3rd pers. with the impf. without ''waw'' in prose are {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}}, but with ''waw consec.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ הָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ָהּ}}; with the jussive in the 2nd and 3rd pers. always {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ הָ}}, and the 1st pers. more often {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} than {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}}, and always {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}}.</ref> (''ăn'')<ref>According to Barth ‘n-haltige Suffixe’ in {{GHGcite|title=Sprachwiss. Untersuchungen}}, Lpz. 1907, p. 1 ff., the connecting element, as in Aramaic, was originally ''in'', which in Hebrew became ''en'' in a closed tone-syllable.</ref> is inserted between the suffix and the verbal stem. Since, however, this syllable always has the tone, the ''ă'' is invariably (except in the 1st pers. sing.) modified to tone-bearing {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}. This is called the ''Nûn energicum''<ref>So König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, i. p. 226.</ref> (less suitably ''demonstrativum'' or ''epentheticum''), and occurs principally (see, however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=10}} ''bis'') in pausal forms of the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְבָֽרֲכֶֽנְהוּ|translate=he will bless him}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=22}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְּקֶ֫נְךָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכַ֫בְּדָ֥נְנִי|translate=he will honour me}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=23}}) is unusual; rarely in the perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽרְכֶךָּ}}. On examples like {{GHGheb|text=דָּנַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGpar|26|g}}, {{GHGpar|59|f}}. In far the greatest number of cases, however, this ''Nûn'' is assimilated to the following consonant ({{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}}), or the latter is lost in pronunciation (so {{GHGheb|text=ה}}), and the ''Nûn'' consequently sharpened.
